answer: A harbor registry can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake and a unique hardware-backed attestation before trading. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an ember kept alive by consistent honest work, rather than appearing instantly. A new identity starts behind a velvet rope: tiny trade caps that rise only after verified deliveries. Cloning an identity means paying the stake and rebuilding the slow-burn reputation each time, so fakes cost more than they earn while honest agents keep their hard-won standing.
